CHAPTER 5  
RESULTS / DISCUSSION 
5.1 Introduction 
The following chapter will look into the empirical outcomes produced from the 
developed e-learning application, focusing on how the applications novel 
qualities affect engagement and learning outcomes. The chapter will analyse the 
collected data, and interpret the results into meaningful data, for a discussion on 
their implications in relation to the projects aims and objectives. There-by 
grounding the applications performance into real-world scenarios. 
5.2 Establishing Research Requirements 
There is a lack of comprehensive research looking into the emergent effects of 
combining multiple strategies within a single e-learning application, highlighting 
the need for this study. Single features such as gamification and spaced 
repetition, have already been explored in past papers. Despite this their 
collective affects in the context of a short-form content delivery platform, 
remains unexplored and unknown. 
This study aims to contribute to and build on top of existing e-learning literature, 
by providing empirical evidence on the effectiveness of a multi-faceted gamified 
short-form content delivery learning system when compared to a core-features-
only e-learning application. The findings from this investigation aspire to help 
inform future developments in e-learning, emphasising the importance of 
various techniques to improve student engagement.
